# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

## From iteration cand_0001 (tau2 airline, tools capability)
- Un-winnable-from-the-edit-space tasks pollute the reward signal. On this suite, 2 of 7 failing tasks (40, 22) fail because the USER SIMULATOR ends the episode with "yes###STOP###" before the agent gets an execution turn. No edit to the agent's TOOL surface (the capability this run owns) can fix a task where the agent never gets a turn to call a tool. Suggestion: let a task/cluster be tagged `out-of-scope-for-capability=<cap>` so the gate can report val EXCLUDING structurally-unreachable tasks, or at least surface "N of the failing tasks are not addressable by this capability" so the optimizer isn't scored (and doesn't burn iterations) against an unreachable ceiling. As-is, the max reachable val is mechanically < the nominal max, and nothing in the provided files states that up front.
- reward_basis is the single most important fact for proposing good edits, and it is only discoverable by digging into trajectory metadata. Suggestion: surface `reward_basis` (e.g. [DB, COMMUNICATE]) per task directly in INSTRUCTIONS.md or the trace summary. Knowing the tool NAME is not graded (only DB state + communicated facts) is what unlocks the composite-wrapper and enriched-return edit classes; an optimizer that misses this wastes effort trying to make the agent call a specific named tool.
- Suggestion: include a tiny per-task `db_match`/`comm_match` breakdown in the failing-trace summaries. This iteration's highest-confidence fix (task 11: DB already correct, only the spoken refund figure wrong) was only findable by manually reconstructing that the DB write passed and just the COMMUNICATE check failed. A pre-computed per-check pass/fail column would let any optimizer instantly spot "COMMUNICATE-only" failures, which are the cheapest, safest flips.
